title: sqliteBinding
responsibility: Converts a model field value to a SQLite binding, serializing JSON and booleans and rejecting incompatible values.

inputs.name: sqliteBinding.value
inputs.description: The application value to encode: `null` passes through as `null` for a nullable field, `json` fields serialize any value that `JSON.stringify` accepts (so a non-nullable `json` field encodes `null` as the text 'null'), and `boolean`, `string`, `number` and `blob` fields need a boolean, a string, a finite number or a Uint8Array respectively. `undefined` is always rejected.
inputs.unknownReason: Application values vary with the field descriptor, which controls the binding checks and conversions.

inputs.name: sqliteBinding.field
inputs.description: The field's SQLite storage type and nullability: `type` selects the encoding and must be `json`, `boolean`, `string`, `number` or `blob` (other types throw unless the value is `null` on a nullable field), and `nullable: true` lets a `null` value pass through as `null`.

outputs.name: sqliteBinding
outputs.description: The value to bind: `null` for a `null` input to a nullable field, the JSON text for `json` fields, `0` or `1` for `boolean` fields, the unchanged string or number for `string` and `number` fields, and the same `Uint8Array` instance (not a copy) for `blob` fields. It is never `undefined`, because unsupported input throws instead.

errors.name: InvalidSqliteFieldValueError
errors.description: Thrown with the message 'Invalid SQLite <type> field value' whenever the value cannot be encoded for the field: `undefined`, a function or symbol in a `json` field, a value of the wrong JavaScript kind (such as a string in a `number` field), `NaN` or an infinite number in a `number` field, and `null` in a non-nullable field other than `json`. Unsupported field types throw with the same message for every value except `null` on a nullable field.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: Propagated unchanged from `JSON.stringify`, which this function does not catch: a `json` field value that is or contains a BigInt or a circular reference throws a TypeError, and a `toJSON` method or getter that throws propagates its own exception.
